name: Apple Silicon Mac, 128 GB unified (M3 Max / M4 Max class)
gpu: integrated, shares the 128 GB unified pool
notes: A class entry, not one SKU: 400 GB/s is the M3 Max, 546 GB/s the M4 Max. Setups listed against this class were reported on either.
Closest structural analogue to DGX Spark — unified memory, so capacity is generous and bandwidth is the limiter — but at roughly 1.5-2x the Spark's 273 GB/s.
Serving path is MLX or llama.cpp/Metal, not SGLang or vLLM: the CUDA-specific forks (DSpark, DFlash2) have no port, so speculative-decoding setups are not comparable across this class and Spark.
Memory pressure is configurable (sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb); default GPU wired limit is well below 128 GB, so large MoE builds need it raised.

Ultra chips exist above this class's recorded range (M2 Ultra 800 GB/s, M3 Ultra 819 GB/s — there is no M4 Ultra). A setup naming an Ultra must say so in its measurement note; do not average Ultra bandwidth into this class.

memory.note: bandwidth is per-chip; this class spans 400-546 GB/s and each variant carries its own figure

compute.note: Neural Engine 38 TOPS is published for the M4 family; earlier generations' NE rates are not restated here. MLX and llama.cpp/Metal primarily drive the GPU; the ANE is largely unused by current local-LLM runtimes.

thermal.note: Apple does not publish chip TDP
